Calculation execution belongs to the shared deterministic calculation and units owner; nothing here is a measurement, evidence, a battery capacity, a statement of what any battery must hold, a runtime, a state of charge, an energy, a charging, chemistry or BMS result, a rating, sizing, selection or suitability of any battery, source, wire, fuse or component, a comparison with any rating, a protection, compatibility or safety statement, or a readiness, progression or validation input. method.model: ONE electrical load, explicitly declared by the inventor, through which ONE DC current I_load (in amperes) stays at one constant value for ONE declared duration t (in hours). Electric current is the flow of electric charge, so while the current stays constant the charge that flows through the load is Q_load (in ampere hours) = I_load × t: exactly zero for a zero current or a zero duration and never negative for a current and a duration that are not negative. The result is the charge of that ideal constant-current relation only, expressed in the ampere hour, a unit of electric charge: not an energy, not a measured, rated, stored, available or deliverable charge, not a battery capacity, a statement of what any battery must hold, a runtime or a state of charge, and not compared with any rating.
method.executed_form: q_load = i_load x t_duration, with i_load in A (not negative) and t_duration in h (not negative), the sign of each decided from the exact decimal value before any binary rounding; evaluated as the exact rational product of the two binary64 inputs rounded once to binary64 and accepted only when it is exactly 0.0 for a zero current or a zero duration, or finite, positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of it; then shown only when it agrees with the exact decimal product I x t of the entered values within a relative error of 2^-51, as that exact value rounded once to 12 significant digits (round half to even) and labelled exact or rounded. No unit is converted: the ampere hour is the product of the declared ampere and hour, and no coulomb, milliampere hour, second or minute is formed.
method.derivation: DOE-HDBK-1011/1-92, Electrical Science, Volume 1, Module ES-01 (Basic Electrical Theory), section Electrical Terminology, subsection Current (printed page ES-01 page 10), identifies electric current with the flow of electric charge and defines one ampere as one coulomb of charge passing a given point per second (DOE-CHG-S1; recorded as electronics_electrical:PR018). InventorAI restates that identification as current being the rate of electric charge flow and, ONLY for a current that stays constant throughout the declared duration t, as the algebraic product Q = I × t; it is not claimed that DOE prints Q = I × t, and no varying-current, average-current, duty-cycle or integration treatment is derived. The coulomb as the SI unit of electric charge (C = s · A) and the ampere hour as a unit of electric charge (1 A · h = 3.6 × 10³ C) follow NIST SP 811 (NIST-AH-S1; recorded as electronics_electrical:PR020); from them the product of an ampere and an hour is the ampere hour, the unit in which this method gives its result, and the conversion factor is recorded for unit identification only and is never applied. The relations are restated independently; no handbook or NIST text, worked example, figure or table is copied, and the relation is not shown to describe the inventor's load.

roles.meaning: the DC current through the load that stays constant for the whole declared duration, as declared by the inventor; not negative; not measured or checked by InventorAI, which does not establish that it is constant (the role written I)

the duration during which that constant current flows, as declared by the inventor, in hours; not negative; not a measured, rated or expected operating time, never a battery runtime and never worked out by InventorAI (the role written t)

the electric charge that flows through the load during the declared constant-current duration, I x t, in ampere hours; exactly zero for a zero current or a zero duration and never negative; a charge, not an energy; never a measured, rated, stored, available or deliverable charge, never a battery capacity, a statement of what any battery must hold, a runtime or a state of charge, and never compared with any rating (the role written Q)

rules: Grammar: strict ASCII decimal - an optional single leading minus, one to nine integer digits, and an optional single fractional part of one to nine digits, for both I and t; no plus sign, exponent, separator, space, Unicode digit, unit suffix, inf, nan or normalization. An omitted, malformed or over-length value is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT, resolved before the shared owner is called.

Representation limits, not physical limits: the digit limits bound what can be typed (I from 0 to below 10^9 A, t from 0 to below 10^9 h, steps of 10^-9); they are not physical limits, equipment ratings, operating times or a claim that such values are realistic, and the 64-character field cap is NON-PHYSICAL abuse protection only.

Current not negative, then duration not negative: the exact decimal value of I must not be negative (otherwise CURRENT_NEGATIVE), and then the exact decimal value of t must not be negative (otherwise DURATION_NEGATIVE), each decided before any binary rounding and with no number. A zero current or a zero duration, including -0, is admitted and gives exactly zero charge, never a negative zero.

Owner applicability: the method record declares no owner condition, because the condition vocabulary holds no not-negative condition and none is added; a negative i_load or t_duration that reaches the method adapter is refused there as FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE (unreachable from the page). No result range is declared.

Binary bridge: each admitted decimal is converted once to the correctly rounded binary64 value; every admitted nonzero value lies between 10^-9 and 10^9 in magnitude, so it is a normal binary64 number with a relative rounding error of at most 2^-53, a value that is not negative stays not negative and a zero I or t stays exactly zero.

Numerical acceptance in the adapter: the exact rational product i_load x t_duration of the binary inputs is rounded once to binary64. A zero current or a zero duration gives exactly 0.0. A nonzero exact result is accepted only when the rounded value is finite, positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of it; overflow, underflow or any failed check is FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no numerical payload, never rewritten as a refusal. Inside the representation limits every nonzero result lies between 10^-18 and 10^18 A·h, so neither overflow nor underflow can occur from the page.

Decimal-reference acceptance in the consumer: a successful owner result is shown only when it is exactly zero (not a negative zero) for an exactly zero current or duration, and otherwise is positive and lies within a relative error of 2^-51 of the exact decimal product I x t of the entered decimals; otherwise the outcome is KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE with no number. The proven worst case for every admitted input is below 3.0000001 x 2^-53.

Display: the accepted result is shown from the exact decimal value, never from the binary value: rounded once to 12 significant digits, round half to even, with trailing zeros removed; it is labelled exact when that rounding changes nothing and rounded otherwise. Plain decimal notation is used from 10^-6 A·h to below 10^12 A·h and the form m x 10^e otherwise, so a tiny nonzero charge is never shown as 0. The digits shown imply no measurement resolution, precision or accuracy.

The result is the ideal constant-current relation only: a current that changes during the duration, on-off, intermittent or duty-cycled operation, standby or sleep phases, start-up or inrush current, switching transients, AC behaviour, several loads or periods, the source's own behaviour as it discharges, temperature effects and conversion losses are not included; no average-current substitution and no integration over a varying current is performed.

disclosure: This is the electric charge that flows through one load while the DC current I you declared stays constant for the whole duration t you declared: Q = I × t, given in ampere hours (A·h).

The current and the duration are your own declared values. InventorAI did not measure them and does not establish that the current is constant: a current that changes, on-off or duty-cycled use, standby or sleep phases, start-up or inrush current, switching, AC behaviour and any load whose current varies are not included, and no average current is substituted.

Q is a charge, not an energy. The ampere hour is a unit of electric charge that is also used in battery ratings, but this value is not compared with any rating: it is not a battery capacity, a runtime, a state of charge, a battery choice or a sizing, selection or suitability statement for any battery or source.
No unit is converted: the current is read in amperes, the duration in hours and the charge is given in ampere hours only, with no milliampere hours, coulombs, seconds or minutes.
The value is shown exactly when it can be; otherwise it is rounded to 12 significant digits and labelled rounded. The digits follow from your entry; they are not the precision of any measurement.

Next engineering need: a charge value alone cannot determine how long a real battery lasts. Whether the current really stays constant, what the load draws over its whole use with every phase included, which source or battery could supply it and how that source behaves as it discharges, and whether the load, its wiring, source and any switch are rated for the current all remain unverified, and must be checked by measurement or a qualified person before any reliance. The result is preliminary, advisory, UNVALIDATED and not evidence.
